variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: `=` performs immediate assignment. `:=` performs delayed assignment. `(* ... *)` for comments.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Everything is a symbolic expression. Exact arithmetic (rationals, infinite precision) is natively supported.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
2 + 3 * 4
2 ^ 10

(* Matrix multiplication *)
mat1 . mat2

(* Element-wise operates automatically *)
{1, 2} * {3, 4}
operators.notes: Dot `.` is used for dot product / matrix multiplication. Most operators thread over lists automatically.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
If[x > 0,
  Print["Positive"],
  Print["Negative or Zero"]
]

(* Piecewise for mathematical definitions *)
f[x_] := Piecewise[{{x^2, x > 0}, {0, True}}]
conditionals.notes: `If` is a function. `Piecewise` is preferred for building mathematical functions with conditions.

for_loop.title: For Loop / Do
for_loop.code:
Do[Print[i^2], {i, 1, 10}]

(* More idiomatic: generating lists *)
squares = Table[i^2, {i, 1, 10}]

(* Functional mapping *)
Map[#^2 &, Range[10]]
for_loop.notes: `Do` and `Table` are standard. Functional paradigms (`Map`, `Apply`) are highly preferred over procedural loops.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: `While` is available but functional alternatives like `Nest` or `FixedPoint` are often more idiomatic.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
(* Definition with pattern matching *)
calculateMean[l_List] := If[Length[l] == 0, Missing[], Total[l] / Length[l]]

(* Pure function (anonymous) *)
square = #^2 &;
functions.notes: Functions are defined via pattern matching `x_`. Pure functions use `#` for arguments and `&` to terminate.

arrays.title: Arrays & Lists
arrays.notes: Lists `{...}` serve as vectors, matrices, and arrays. Accessed using `Part` or `[[...]]`.

maps.title: Associations (Maps)
maps.notes: `Association` provides high-performance key-value maps. Queries on them are highly optimized.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
Check[
  1 / 0,
  Print["An error occurred!"]
]

(* Catch and Throw *)
Catch[
  If[x < 0, Throw["Negative value"]]
]
error_handling.notes: `Check` monitors for messages. `Catch` and `Throw` allow non-local control flow for exceptions.

comments.title: Comments & Headers
comments.code:
# Comment in Wolfram Language
# Multi-line comments or docstrings
# are documented here
comments.notes: Wolfram Language uses # or language-specific delimiters (% in MATLAB, ! in Fortran) for comments.

numbers.title: Vectors, Matrices & Numbers
numbers.notes: Wolfram Language is optimized for vector and matrix calculations with high-precision numerical representations.

booleans.title: Logical Vectors & Booleans
booleans.code:
is_valid = TRUE
flags = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
booleans.notes: Wolfram Language provides boolean types with support for element-wise vector logic operations.

type_casting.title: Type Coercion & Casting
type_casting.notes: Wolfram Language converts data between numeric, character, factor, and logical representations.

strings.title: Strings & Character Vectors
strings.notes: Wolfram Language treats strings as atomic character scalars or vector arrays.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Wolfram Language formats numerical output with sprintf formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Conditionals & Switches
pattern_matching.notes: Wolfram Language executes branch logic via switch, ifelse, or conditional filtering.

range.title: Sequences & Indexing
range.notes: Wolfram Language indexes matrices and vectors using 1-based indexing and sequence generators.

iterators.title: Vectorized Apply & Iteration
iterators.notes: Wolfram Language emphasizes vectorized functional processing (apply, map) over explicit loops.

oop_classes.title: Object Systems & S3/S4
oop_classes.code:
# Object systems in Wolfram Language
obj = list(name = "Model", score = 0.95)
class(obj) = "metric"
oop_classes.notes: Wolfram Language uses class dispatch systems (S3/S4 in R, multiple dispatch in Julia) for data modeling.

lists.title: DataFrames & Lists
lists.notes: Wolfram Language stores heterogeneous columnar records in data frames and lists.

tuples.title: Pairs & Records
tuples.notes: Wolfram Language uses named vectors or lightweight structures for data records.

sets.title: Set Operations
sets.notes: Wolfram Language provides native mathematical set functions (union, intersect, setdiff).

modules_import.title: Libraries & Packages
modules_import.notes: Wolfram Language loads package namespaces using library or import declarations.
